# Convergence: 8b0ab63b190ae2b5eab304a7bf009d5d1acbdfc8

Branch `worktree-wp-git-boundary` (worktree `.claude/worktrees/wp-git-boundary`), off origin/main b56bc276a. Trail #494. Not pushed.

## Scope landed (slice A of the Git boundary brief)

- `GitRemote` (callisto-model `vcs/remote.rs`): every remote command gets the remote name (`ls-remote -- <name>`, `push -- <name>`, `ls-remote --symref -- <name> HEAD`, `symbolic-ref refs/remotes/<name>/HEAD`). Binding is a `SemanticInputDigest` of the name plus every fetch and push URL from one `git remote -v` (same output as `get-url --all` / `--push --all`, rewrites applied; verified with insteadOf, pushInsteadOf and two pushurls). Rechecked before each effect. GitHub classification of push URLs only for forge features. URLs have no Display; Debug prints `RemoteUrls(..)`.
- Removed: `canonical_git_remote` (url::Url parse and rewrite), `PreparedGitRemote`, `programs::GIT_REMOTE`, the HTTPS/SSH-only, owner/repo-path, git-account and GitHub-parse refusals.
- Kept: E132 for a URL with a password, or a user name or query over HTTP(S). Reason: intents record a digest of the URLs, and a digest of a guessable password is recoverable by guessing.
- Env policy: `vcs::GIT_ENVIRONMENT` (GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, LC_ALL=C) applied by `CliCommandRunner` to every git child (run, run_quiet/timeout, run_with_stdin, run_with_env). Before: none set. Pager: unreachable (stdout is always a pipe), not set. core.quotepath: every parsed path list uses `-z`, so not set. Color: only `git grep` colors under user config (verified), so `--no-color` on it.
- Old intents: E124 with reason "a package's release inputs differ ... or Callisto 0.22.0 or earlier planned the intent". Changeset `.changeset/radiant-wolves-swim.md` (patch, with **Action:**).

## Split (not in this commit)

Slice B, its own PR: `Rev` (CommitSha or refs/tags|heads/<name>, HEAD) for read_at, commit_time, resolve_commit, path_exists_at, files_containing_at, commits_since (+ CommitWalker) and callers; one `GitPath` (Pathspec::literal + check_ignore_arg); `git add` into GitAccess (apply.rs, pre.rs). Estimated ~500 changed lines; slice A is ~1,620.

## Passes

1. Classes: secrets in output, foreign-grammar parsing, preview/real same structure, consumers of changed items, process counts. Found: get-url twice per recheck added a git process per tag operation; recheck test deleted without replacement; the query-string credential refusal dropped. Changed: one `git remote -v`; recheck test restored on the new runner; query over HTTP(S) refused.
2. Classes: help text naming the wrong URL (open finding error.rs:362), local-path origin rejected in preview (resolved finding derive.rs:309), hardcoded remote name, swallowed errors, unwrap/expect, edge inputs (remote named `-x`, tabs, `file://`, helpers `hg::`). Found: E132 help named only HTTPS/SSH; errors.md row stale; clippy map_err_ignore in init. Changed: E132 help names both get-url commands; errors.md; `expect` naming the semver invariant; comment on the one swallowed parse error.
3. Gate-driven: e2e harness fake git rejected `--` and read the refspec by position; real-push mode substituted URL arguments. Changed: harness accepts `--`, reads the last argument, and rewrites with `-c url.<bare>.insteadOf` for push/ls-remote only.
4. Mutation (`cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff` on remote.rs): 11 missed, then 2 after adding classification, Debug and name assertions. Remaining 2 are `url_tags`, covered by callisto-graph `resolve_release_commit_*` tests across the crate boundary.
5. Full pass over the final diff: clean.

## Gate (final tree, unsandboxed, exit codes)

- just pre-push: 0
- just lint: 0
- just doc-check: 0
- just test: 0
- just fuzz-check: 0
and the repository exists.

Pre-push self-review checklist (from recurring Entire reviewer findings). Check your full diff against every item; fix or justify each before reporting. Every push triggers a paid review: do not push until the lead says so.

1. Secrets: no user-supplied URL, remote, token, env value or path that may carry credentials is printed in any message, error, JSON or log. Print only values we derived ourselves (owner/repo slug, package names). Child processes get the runner's filtered environment.
2. Same structure for preview and real: dry runs, hints and previews compute on exactly the set/plan the real command uses (selection, group expansion, publishable packages, roster). No second derivation.
3. Modes: text vs --format json vs non-TTY. JSON stdout stays a single document; human notes go to stderr once in both modes; json never prompts. Check every new message in all three modes.
4. Validation order: mode/eligibility first, then input validation, then prompts or side effects. A bad input never reaches a confirmation screen.
5. Optional conveniences (preselection, detection, previews, hints) degrade with a warning; they never make the command fail.
6. Never parse text we rendered, and never hand-parse a foreign grammar (Markdown, git URLs, shell) beyond the coarse classification we need; prefer the owning tool or omit.
7. Rust: exhaustive match on our own enums (no _ arm); no unwrap outside tests; expect names its invariant; no swallowed errors (.ok(), drop(result)) without a one-line reason; no process::exit outside main; Drop-based cleanup; no global mutable state unless unavoidable; minimal visibility.
8. Edge inputs for anything touching user paths or strings: spaces, newlines, leading ':' or '-', unicode, empty, very long.
9. Tests: one test per behaviour through the real binary where users see it; tests clean up children and temp files on failure.
11. Consumers: for every function, field, type or enum variant whose behaviour or meaning you changed, list every reader (rg the name across crates, including the changelog, version planner, release preview, PR body, JSON reports and tests) and confirm each still gets what it expects. A value with two jobs must be split, not repurposed.
10. Precedent: when a behaviour has a well-known precedent (git, cargo, npm, changesets), follow it and cite it rather than inventing.

- GitPath replaces Pathspec::literal, Pathspec::excluded and check_ignore_arg, with each command's spelling of a literal path inside it.

- The user-typed --since expression is resolved in GitAccess::merge_base_with_head, after --end-of-options.
- The version checkpoint methods drop their ref-name argument: there is one checkpoint ref.
- Tests run real git against a tag named -x, names with revision syntax, and paths with a leading colon or dash, spaces, newlines and glob characters.
